description: Fault detection and handling for the demo cluster. One panel per sample app + cluster-level health stats + K8sGPT activity signals.

options.content:
### Sample apps — `demo-apps` namespace (instrumented with golden signals)

| App | Stack | Limit | /metrics | Role | Fault trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 `payments-api`   | Go     | 128Mi | ✓ | **OOMKill victim**     | `./scripts/trigger-oomkill.sh` → allocates past the limit in the running container after every restart → CrashLoopBackOff |
| 🟡 `recommend-svc`  | Python | 128Mi + 128Mi `leak-fixture` sidecar | ✓ | **Slow-leak victim**   | `./scripts/trigger-slowleak.sh` → the sidecar's memory climbs 20 MB/min until it is OOMKilled (invisible to K8sGPT until then) |
| 🟢 `catalog-svc`    | nginx  | 64Mi  | — | **Healthy control**    | none — no traffic, always green |
| ⚙️ `loadgen`        | curl   | 32Mi  | — | **Traffic generator**  | runs continuously, ~2 req/sec each to payments-api and recommend-svc `/healthz` |

### Detection layers

- **Golden signals (L · T · E · S)** — Throughput / Latency / Errors panels show signs of fault *regardless of root cause*. The Composite Health Score combines them into one 0-100 number — the always-on, root-cause-agnostic detector.
- **K8sGPT** (`k8sgpt-system`) — scans the `demo-apps` Pods and writes a Result per finding (`kubectl get results -n k8sgpt-system`). With an LLM configured it adds an AI explanation; with a Slack webhook it posts each new Result. Specific, after-the-fact.
- **watcher** (`k8sgpt-system`) — writes a Result when a ConfigMap labelled `k8sgpt-detection-pack.io/critical=true` is created, changed or deleted.

### Observability — `monitoring` namespace

- **kube-prometheus-stack** — Prometheus (6h retention) + Grafana + Alertmanager + kube-state-metrics + node-exporter. App `/metrics` scraped via per-app **ServiceMonitor**.
- Dashboards auto-loaded via Grafana sidecar; source: `demo-cluster/grafana/demo-cluster-overview.json`.

panels.title: Demo apps healthy
panels.description: Number of pods in demo-apps currently Ready

panels.title: CrashLoopBackOff
panels.description: Containers currently waiting in CrashLoopBackOff. Falls back to 0 when no pods match — keeps the panel showing a green '0' instead of 'No data' when everything is healthy.

panels.title: OOMKills (last 5m)
panels.description: Restarts attributable to OOM (container had OOMKilled state × number of restarts in window). The naive increase() on the OOMKilled gauge can't handle rapid CrashLoop cycles — this query is robust to that.

targets.expr: sum(max_over_time(kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason{namespace="demo-apps", reason="OOMKilled"}[5m]) * on(pod, container) group_left increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="demo-apps"}[5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Restarts (last 5m)
panels.description: Total container restarts in demo-apps within the last 5 minutes

panels.title: Restart rate per pod (1m window)
panels.description: rate(restarts/sec). Goes high during CrashLoopBackOff cycles, returns to 0 when stable. The cleanest live signal of an ongoing fault.

targets.expr: topk(6, (sum by (namespace, pod, container) (rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="demo-apps"}[1m])) and on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="demo-apps", phase="Running"} == 1))) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Container restart events / min
panels.description: increase(restart_total)[1m] per pod, rendered as bars. Each bar is a new container restart in that minute. In this demo the OOMKill victim restarts only when OOMed, so this also functions as an OOMKill rate panel — but it's robust to kube-state-metrics' sparse emission of the OOMKilled gauge during long backoff. Drops to 0 once the pod stabilizes.

targets.expr: topk(6, (sum by (namespace, pod, container) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="demo-apps"}[1m])) and on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="demo-apps", phase="Running"} == 1))) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Container restarts over time
panels.description: Restart count per pod. Climbing here means CrashLoopBackOff — the signal K8sGPT's Pod analyzer flags.

targets.expr: topk(6, (sum by (namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="demo-apps"}) and on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="demo-apps", phase="Running"} == 1))) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Active fault states (empty = healthy ✓)
panels.description: Containers in demo-apps currently in a waiting state (CrashLoopBackOff / ImagePullBackOff / ErrImagePull / ContainerCreating). When the cluster is healthy this is just a green checkmark — that's the goal state. During a fault the table populates with one row per affected pod, color-coded by reason. These are exactly the events K8sGPT's Pod analyzer flags.

panels.title: Memory growth rate (per pod, 2m window)
panels.description: rate() of container_memory_working_set_bytes — the SLOPE of the memory line, in bytes/sec. The cleanest live signal of a slow leak: visible at any absolute memory level. Negative values during OOM cycles are kernel reclaim, not anomalies. Thresholds: yellow ≥ 100 KB/s (~6 MB/min), red ≥ 500 KB/s (~30 MB/min).

targets.expr: topk(6, (deriv(sum by (namespace, pod, container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="demo-apps", container!="", container!="POD"})[2m:15s]) and on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="demo-apps", phase="Running"} == 1))) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Composite Health Score (0-100, lower = worse)
panels.description:
Aggregate health score, 0-100 (higher = healthier). Read the score AND the hover on which term is firing.

Formula (each term is subtracted independently, so multiple hits stack):
  100 (baseline)
  −50 · CrashLoopBackOff on any demo-apps container
  −20 · memory working-set > 50% of limit (any container)
  −30 · memory working-set > 80% of limit (any container)
  −30 · payments-api HTTP 5xx rate > 1% (1m window)
  −30 · recommend-svc HTTP 5xx rate > 1% (1m window)
  −50 · any demo-apps pod not Ready (payments-api / recommend-svc / catalog-svc)

Colour bands:
  ≥ 70 = green (healthy)
  40–69 = yellow (degraded)
  <  40 = red (critical)

The whole point of this panel: detect any of the demo's faults
without knowing the root cause. When it turns red, drill down to the
LTES row below to see which golden signal is affected.

targets.expr: 100 - (((sum(kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{namespace="demo-apps", reason="CrashLoopBackOff"} == 1) or vector(0)) > bool 0) * 50) - (((max(sum by(namespace, pod, container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="demo-apps", container!="", container!="POD"}) / on(namespace, pod, container) sum by(namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="demo-apps", resource="memory"})) or vector(0)) > bool 0.5) * 20) - (((max(sum by(namespace, pod, container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="demo-apps", container!="", container!="POD"}) / on(namespace, pod, container) sum by(namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="demo-apps", resource="memory"})) or vector(0)) > bool 0.8) * 30) - (((sum(rate(payments_api_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[1m])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(payments_api_http_requests_total[1m])), 0.001) or vector(0)) > bool 0.01) * 30) - (((sum(rate(recommend_svc_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[1m])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(recommend_svc_http_requests_total[1m])), 0.001) or vector(0)) > bool 0.01) * 30) - (((min(kube_pod_status_ready{namespace="demo-apps", pod=~"(payments-api|recommend-svc|catalog-svc)-.*", condition="true"}) or vector(1)) < bool 1) * 50)

panels.title: Throughput — req/sec (T)
panels.description: Golden signal T: rate of HTTP requests per second, per service. Generated by the loadgen pod. Drops to 0 while the service's scrape target is down.

panels.title: Latency p95 — ms (L)
panels.description: Golden signal L: 95th percentile request latency, per service. Spikes during load saturation and during fault recovery cycles. Drops to 0 while the service's scrape target is down.

targets.expr: ((histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(payments_api_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m]))) * 1000) and on() (avg(up{job="payments-api"}) == 1)) or on() vector(0)
((histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(recommend_svc_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m]))) * 1000) and on() (avg(up{job="recommend-svc"}) == 1)) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Service errors — % (E)
panels.description: Golden signal E. Combines two failure modes: (a) HTTP 5xx responses emitted by the app itself, and (b) Prometheus scrape unavailability (`up == 0`) — the only signal that catches OOMKill / CrashLoop / pod-down faults where the server never gets a chance to emit a 5xx because the connection is refused. catalog-svc uses kube_pod_status_ready since it has no /metrics endpoint. 100% means target was unreachable for the entire window.

panels.title: Saturation — memory % of limit (S)
panels.description: Golden signal S: each container's memory working set as % of its memory limit (top 6, running pods only). Memory only: it is the resource every demo fault exhausts. A container OOMKilled in the last minute shows as 100%: memory is sampled about every 15 s, so the sample at the moment of the kill is usually missed. The red dashed line is the 100% limit; it is always drawn, so the y-axis always reaches 100%.

targets.expr: topk(6, (max by (namespace, pod, container) (  container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="demo-apps", pod=~"(payments-api|recommend-svc|catalog-svc)-.*", container!="", container!="POD"}   / on(namespace, pod, container) group_left   kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="demo-apps", resource="memory"}   * 100  or 100 * (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{namespace="demo-apps", pod=~"(payments-api|recommend-svc|catalog-svc)-.*", reason="OOMKilled"} == 1)   and on(namespace, pod, container) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="demo-apps"}[1m]) > 0)) and on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="demo-apps", phase="Running"} == 1)))

panels.title: K8sGPT detection events (per minute)
panels.description: Each bar marks WHEN K8sGPT created a new Result (and, with Slack on, posted it) — bar height = number of new Result CRDs that landed in that 1-minute window. Flat-zero baseline means no recent detections; vertical spikes are the exact moments the agent fired. More telling than a cumulative count: when you trigger OOMKill at T+10s and a bar appears at ~T+30s, you see the agent reacting in real time. Sourced from delta(k8sgpt_number_of_results[1m]), clamped to 0 to suppress the dips when Result CRDs are garbage-collected.

panels.title: K8sGPT diagnoses by Kind
panels.description: Currently-active K8sGPT Result CRDs grouped by the Kubernetes Kind that triggered them (Pod, Service, Deployment, etc.). When the cluster is healthy this is empty. During a fault each row is one K8sGPT finding (with an AI explanation when an LLM is configured). Refreshes from k8sgpt_number_of_results_by_type emitted by the operator.

panels.title: LLM calls — errors + latency
panels.description:
Two correlated signals for the K8sGPT → LLM path, on a shared time axis:
• Errors (left Y-axis, ops/sec) — failed LLM calls and reconcile errors averaged over 5m. Spikes during rate-limiting, auth failures, or network issues to the provider.
• Avg latency (right Y-axis, seconds) — mean reconcile duration from controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds. The LLM round-trip dominates this, so it's effectively the LLM call latency. Healthy is a few seconds or less on a small hosted model; climbing latency without errors usually means the model is throttled but still serving.
Watching both together reveals the failure mode: errors spike + latency steady = hard rejection (429/auth); latency climbs first then errors = the LLM is dying slowly.

panels.title: K8sGPT agent — health + golden signals (LTES)
panels.description:
Composite 0-100 health score plus the four golden signals for the K8sGPT operator itself:
• Health — 100 minus 30 per active error mode (failed AI calls / reconcile errors above 0.1/s, sustained 5m).
• Throughput — reconciles/sec for the k8sgpt controller (controller_runtime_reconcile_total). Drops to 0 if the controller is stuck.
• Latency — average reconcile duration (controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds). Long reconciles mean the LLM round-trip is slow.
• Errors — combined rate of failed LLM calls + reconcile errors per second. Spikes during rate-limiting or auth failures.
• Saturation — active_workers / max_concurrent_reconciles, as a percentage. Pegs at 100% when the controller's worker pool is fully busy. With K8sGPT's default max=1, you see this hold at 100% while an LLM call is in flight — slow LLM = sustained saturation.
This is the agent's own watchdog — does the agent work, not whether the cluster is healthy.

targets.expr: sum(clamp_min(100 - 30 * ((rate(k8sgpt_number_of_failed_backend_ai_calls[5m]) > bool 0.1) or vector(0)) - 30 * ((rate(k8sgpt_reconcile_error_count[5m]) > bool 0.1) or vector(0)), 0))

properties.value: Composite 0-100 score for the K8sGPT agent. 100 = no errors. Subtracts 30 per active error mode (failed AI calls / reconcile errors) when either exceeds 0.1/s averaged over 5 minutes. The agent's own watchdog — separate from the cluster's health.

Throughput. A 'reconcile' is one iteration of the K8sGPT controller's main work loop — it wakes up when a watched resource changes (or on a periodic tick), scans the cluster, calls the LLM (when configured), writes Result CRDs, and posts to Slack (when configured). This is the rate of those iterations per second. K8sGPT's controller-runtime default re-sync is ~10 minutes, so 0 in a 5-minute window during idle is normal (shown as blue, not red). Only worry if it's still 0 during an active fault. Source: controller_runtime_reconcile_total{controller="k8sgpt"}.

Latency. Average duration of a single reconcile, in seconds. Mostly dominated by the LLM round-trip — slow LLM = climbing latency here. Healthy is a few seconds or less on a small hosted model; far longer usually means the provider is rate-limiting or the model is overloaded. 0 during idle just means no recent reconciles to measure (shown as blue, not green — green would imply 'fast', but there's nothing to be fast at). Source: controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds_sum / count.

Errors. Combined rate of two failure types per second: failed LLM calls (k8sgpt_number_of_failed_backend_ai_calls — rate limits, auth issues, network drops) AND controller reconcile errors (k8sgpt_reconcile_error_count — anything the controller couldn't process). Both feed the Health composite. Spikes during quota burn.

Saturation. Percentage of the controller's worker pool currently busy: active_workers / max_concurrent_reconciles × 100. K8sGPT defaults to max=1 worker, so this is 0% idle or 100% busy. Holds at 100% while an LLM call is in flight — sustained 100% means slow LLM is bottlenecking throughput even if errors are low.
